title: Running HGS Safely in Plain English
summary: Understand why guarded-fabric operations must preserve both availability and the security policy that decides which hosts can unlock protected workloads.
plain_language_explanation: HGS is both an availability dependency and a trust authority. Routine patching, host refresh, certificate renewal and policy maintenance must therefore keep the service reachable without casually weakening attestation just to make a host pass. A production change is successful only when protected VMs can still start on authorized hosts and unauthorized configurations remain blocked.
quick_check: Why is temporarily relaxing HGS attestation after a patch not an acceptable default recovery action?

title: HGS Patching, Monitoring and Attestation-Policy Lifecycle
summary: Operate HGS through cumulative updates, policy changes and guarded-host refreshes with explicit sequencing, monitoring and rollback evidence.
objective: Explain how to patch and monitor HGS while controlling attestation-policy drift and preserving the ability of compliant guarded hosts to attest.
body_outline: Microsoft recommends keeping HGS current and, when patching the guarded fabric, updating Hyper-V hosts before HGS so new host measurements are available before HGS policy changes are activated.

TPM attestation depends on host-specific TPM identifiers plus approved TPM baselines and code-integrity policies; hardware, firmware and software lifecycle events can therefore require controlled policy updates.
Trusted TPM root/intermediate certificates are part of TPM authenticity validation and may vary across hardware vendors or TPM models.

New or changed attestation policies introduced by servicing should be reviewed before they are enabled; passing attestation must never be achieved by indiscriminately disabling locked or security-relevant controls.
Operational monitoring should distinguish HGS service availability, endpoint/TLS health, policy state, host attestation outcomes and shielded-workload start failures.
quick_check: What evidence should be captured before approving a new TPM baseline after firmware maintenance?

title: HGS Backup, Restore, Key Custody and Complete-Cluster Recovery
summary: Design recoverability for HGS state and cryptographic keys without relying on an ordinary server-image restore model.
objective: Explain what must be preserved to recover an HGS cluster and why loss of its original key material can transfer recovery work back to individual VM owners.
body_outline: HGS recovery requires current attestation policies plus the signing and encryption key material used by key protection; these artifacts are security-sensitive and must be stored separately and securely.

Microsoft does not recommend relying on full system-image restore of an HGS node for complete-cluster loss; the preferred pattern is to build a new HGS node/cluster and restore HGS state and required private keys.

State export does not automatically preserve every surrounding dependency such as HGS service name, Active Directory objects or SSL certificates, so recovery documentation must capture those separately.
Certificates added by thumbprint may restore only public information through HGS state; private-key recovery remains dependent on the issuing CA, software-backed key backup or HSM access model.
If original HGS guardian keys cannot be restored, shielded VMs may require their owners to authorize replacement guardian keys before startup is possible.
quick_check: Why can a technically healthy replacement HGS cluster still fail to start existing shielded VMs?

title: Shielding Data, Owner Guardians, Trusted Fabrics and Recovery Authority
summary: Connect tenant-controlled shielding data and guardian ownership to deployment, migration and disaster-recovery decisions for protected workloads.
architecture_notes: Shielding data is created by the VM owner or tenant on a trusted system and can contain secrets, the chosen security level, the owner guardian, trusted host guardians and signed-template information. This means protected-workload recovery is intentionally not controlled solely by fabric administrators. Primary and DR fabrics should be authorized deliberately, with owner-key custody and guardian metadata treated as recoverability assets.
failure_modes: owner guardian or owner key unavailable during last-resort recovery
DR fabric omitted from trusted guardians before an outage
shielding-data file stored insecurely or exposed to fabric administrators
template trust changed without regenerating or validating shielding data
replacement HGS keys not authorized by workload owners
security level chosen without understanding operational restrictions
recovery runbook assumes fabric admin can unilaterally unshield or re-key a tenant-owned VM
enterprise_design_notes: Maintain clear separation between fabric operations and VM-owner authority. Treat owner keys, shielding data, guardian metadata and HGS recovery keys as distinct controlled assets with tested custody, documented DR authorization and auditable change processes.

title: Read-Only HGS Production Lifecycle and Recovery Readiness Pack
summary: Collect patching, policy, TPM-artifact, endpoint and recovery evidence without changing attestation state, exporting private keys or modifying protected VMs.
objective: Produce a timestamped production-readiness pack before HGS servicing, policy maintenance or recovery testing is approved.
steps: Record HGS service version/configuration, current trust mode and published endpoints.
Enumerate enabled/disabled attestation policies and identify whether any new policy awaits security review.
Inventory TPM hosts, baselines and code-integrity policy registrations appropriate to the active TPM design.
Record certificate metadata and expiry for HGS signing, encryption and HTTPS/TLS dependencies without exporting private keys.
Record the date and custody location of the latest HGS state/key backup evidence without opening sensitive backup material.
From representative guarded hosts, capture current attestation diagnostics and compare against the approved maintenance baseline.
Document unresolved drift or recovery blockers before any patch, trust-mode, key or policy change is authorized.
expected_result: A read-only lifecycle/recovery evidence pack with no policy mutation, key export, host authorization, trust-mode change or VM protection change.

title: HGS Post-Patch, Policy Drift and Recovery Failure Decision Tree
summary: Diagnose production HGS failures while preserving the trust boundary and avoiding destructive or security-weakening shortcuts.
diagnostic_order: Classify the incident as HGS service outage, endpoint/TLS failure, attestation regression after host maintenance, policy drift, key-protection failure or DR restore failure.
Preserve exact HGS and guarded-host diagnostics before any policy or key change.
For TPM regressions, compare platform identifier, trusted TPM chain, TPM baseline and code-integrity evidence against the pre-change approved state.
For restore failures, confirm HGS state was imported, required private signing/encryption keys are available to every needed node, and endpoint/service-name dependencies match the recovery plan.
For shielded-VM startup failure after HGS rebuild, verify whether original guardian keys were restored or whether the workload owner must authorize replacement keys.
Escalate with evidence if resolving the issue requires trust-mode, attestation-policy, certificate/private-key, guardian or shielding-data changes.
escalation_boundary: Do not disable security-relevant attestation policy, change trust mode, replace HGS signing/encryption keys, import unverified policy state, expose private keys, modify shielding data or unshield a protected VM as a troubleshooting shortcut without approved security/change authority.

title: HGS Production Operations and Recovery Assessment
summary: Scenario assessment covering patch sequencing, TPM policy lifecycle, backup/recovery, guardian ownership and safe incident decisions.

assessment_items.question: Why should guarded Hyper-V hosts normally be updated before HGS during guarded-fabric servicing?
assessment_items.answer: It lets updated hosts produce the measurements needed by any new or changed HGS attestation policies before those policies are enabled, reducing the chance of policy-induced outage.

assessment_items.question: What two core categories must a complete HGS recovery preserve?
assessment_items.answer: Attestation policy/state and the signing/encryption key material needed for key protection; surrounding dependencies such as TLS certificates, service naming and administrative records also need documented recovery handling.

assessment_items.question: Why is a full server-image backup not the preferred complete-cluster HGS recovery strategy?
assessment_items.answer: Microsoft recommends rebuilding HGS and restoring HGS state plus required key material rather than treating an HGS node like an ordinary image-restored application server.

assessment_items.question: Who ultimately controls authorization of replacement guardian keys for an existing shielded VM?
assessment_items.answer: The VM owner through the owner guardian/owner-controlled recovery material, which preserves separation from fabric administrators.

title: Senior HGS Interview: Patching, TPM Lifecycle, Key Recovery and Tenant Authority
summary: Senior production scenarios testing guarded-fabric servicing, attestation drift, cryptographic recovery and owner/fabric separation.

questions.question: After firmware updates, several TPM-attested hosts fail while others pass. What is your evidence-first sequence?
answer_points: preserve HGS and host diagnostics
compare TPM/platform identity
compare trusted TPM chain
compare measured boot baseline
compare code-integrity policy
review approved firmware change
do not weaken policy simply to restore attestation

questions.question: Your entire HGS cluster is lost. What makes recovery complete rather than merely rebuilding three servers?
answer_points: restore attestation state/policies
restore original signing and encryption private keys or HSM access
recreate service/DNS/TLS dependencies
restore administrative custody records
validate representative host attestation
prove existing shielded VM startup
document owner action if original guardian keys are unavailable

questions.question: Why should owner keys and shielding data stay outside routine fabric-admin custody?
answer_points: they preserve tenant/VM-owner authority
they can contain sensitive provisioning secrets
owner guardian supports last-resort recovery and reauthorization
fabric compromise should not automatically grant workload-secret access
separation of duties is part of the threat model

questions.question: A replacement HGS works for new shielded VMs but old ones do not start. What is the leading design hypothesis?
answer_points: replacement guardian keys differ from the original authorized keys
old VM key protectors do not authorize the new guardian
VM owner may need to reauthorize using owner recovery material
verify restored key material before changing protected workloads
do not unshield as a shortcut
